subject: MAP & ramp: milestone schedule, overage workflow and rate clarifications
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@acmeanalytics.com>, Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & ramp: milestone schedule, overage workflow and rate clarifications

Hi Maya / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attached is a cleaned-up MAP draft (MAP-v1.2.pdf) plus our current rate card (ratecard-2026-04.xlsx). High level ask: we want to align on milestone dates and define an overage/burst workflow that avoids surprise charges while you’re in the evaluation and early ramp phases.

Proposed milestones (please review):
- Week 0: SOW signed & PO issued
- 30 days: POC (functional check, 200k tokens/day, limited dataset)
- 90 days: Pilot (production slice, up to 10M tokens/month)
- Month 6: Full ramp to committed baseline (50M tokens/month)

Questions we need your feedback on:
1) Buffer tolerance: do you want a fixed % buffer over committed baseline (we suggest 20%) or explicit soft caps during the pilot?
2) Overage measurement window: calendar month or trailing 30 days?
3) Burst handling: do you prefer an automatic burst allowance with post-facto billing or a hard cap with rejections?

Our default commercial model we recommend for MAPs is: a monthly measurement window, automatic soft-burst allowance up to 20% of committed volume for the first two billing cycles (surge credit applies), then billed overage at tiered per-token rates. See the ratecard for exact tiers. If you'd like, we can propose a variation that waives charges for up to two surges during pilot.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached MAP and mark any milestone/date edits (I added an editable copy to the thread).
- Procurement: let us know preferred PO cadence and any contracting special terms.
- If acceptable, we’ll convert the MAP to a milestone-based SOW and provide a DocuSign packet for signatures.

Thanks — I’ve looped in Jonas (billing) and Stephanie (solutions) for technical and commercial questions.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[e] evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | [m] +1-415-555-0123

From: Maya Patel <maya@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & ramp: milestone schedule, overage workflow and rate clarifications

Thanks, Evelyn — appreciate the clear draft. A few clarifying questions from our side before we mark the MAP: 

- Measurement window: Is the overage calculated on a calendar-month basis by default? If so, how do you treat partial months during ramp (e.g., if the PO starts mid-month)?
- Burst vs new token: We want to understand what counts toward bursts. If a user hits the same cached conversation repeatedly, does that count as new tokens for billing?
- Surge credit: Can you confirm the exact token allowance for the “first two surges”? We expect to run 2–3 spikes during pilot and want those captured.

Procurement: we’ll need the ratecard called out in the SOW and also prefer that overage be invoiced only after exceeding 120% of committed baseline for two consecutive billing cycles (to avoid one-off spikes). Is that a workable concession?

Also attaching a redline (acme-map-edits.docx) with small date edits and a procurement comment about PO terms. Please advise and happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

—Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics
[m] +1-650-555-9876

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@acmeanalytics.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & ramp: milestone schedule, overage workflow and rate clarifications

Hi Maya — quick notes addressing each of your points (pulled from the ratecard and internal billing rules):

1) Measurement window
- Default: calendar-month billing (1st–last of month).
- Partial-month start: pro-rate the committed baseline for that partial period; overages are calculated against the pro-rated baseline for that partial month.

2) What counts as token volume / burst definition
- Billed tokens = generated tokens + model input tokens as reported by our runtime. Cache hits that avoid re-generation (server-side prefix/KV cache) will not double-bill tokens; however repeated requests that generate output each time are counted.
- We can add a clarification in SOW about server-side prefix caching: requests that are served from the prefix/KV cache and return identical streaming outputs are excluded from additional billing.

3) Surge credit and billing tolerance
- We can offer the following pilot protection: waive overage charges for the first two surges up to 15% of the monthly committed volume (per billing cycle). After that, overages billed at the published tiered rates.
- If Acme wants the 120% / two-consecutive-cycle requirement for invoicing overages, we can support that as a negotiated term for enterprise SOWs — tradeoff is a smaller introductory discount on committed unit price. If you accept the 120% for two cycles rule, we’ll document that in the SOW and adjust the committed pricing by 3% (simple example; final discount to be confirmed).

4) Rate card specifics (summary)
- Tiers: up to committed baseline: included in commit price.
- 0–20% over baseline: burst tier A — $0.0020 / 1k tokens.
- 20–100% over baseline: burst tier B — $0.0045 / 1k tokens.
- >100% over baseline: sustained overage tier C — $0.0090 / 1k tokens.
(See attached ratecard-2026-04.xlsx for exact per-model variations and region adjustments.)

5) Operational fallback during surges
- If you prefer hard rejection over automatic bursts, we can set a hard cap during pilot and flip to soft-burst behavior on Day 1 of full ramp. Let us know which you prefer; default is soft-burst with logging and throttling to respect latency SLOs.

Next steps I recommend:
- Evelyn: incorporate the redline into MAP and add the 120% two-cycle option as a checkbox (indicate the pricing trade-off).
- Maya / Procurement: indicate whether you want pro-rate rule or prefer subscription start aligned to calendar month.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to finalize these items.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Billing & Pricing, Redwood Inference
[e] jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: MAP & ramp: milestone schedule, overage workflow and rate clarifications

Thanks, Jonas and Evelyn — this is very helpful. Procurement reviewed the redline and the 120% / two-cycle rule is acceptable provided the 3% price adjustment is applied as noted. Acme also prefers calendar-month billing if our PO start date falls within five business days of month start; otherwise we request the pro-rate approach.

We’ve attached our edits (acme-map-edits.docx) and approve moving to an SOW with the negotiated checkbox: 120% two-cycle overage invoicing + 3% committed-price adjustment; pilot surge credits as you proposed. Please send the updated SOW and DocuSign packet and we’ll circulate internally for signatures.

If you can send the DocuSign link today, that would speed approval.

Best,
